_comment: Which injectable model error source is covered by which sensitivity table.
哪个可注入的模型误差源由哪张敏感度表覆盖。
Why this file exists. A sensitivity table is a snapshot: it says 'on the day we ran it, these eleven
sources had these effects'. The failure it cannot see is the twelfth source -- someone adds a knob to the
plant or the HAL, the table keeps passing, and the claim keeps being published as if the new knob were
covered. The README's L3 row rests on this table, so 'a new knob must enter the table' has to be a gate.
本文件存在的理由。敏感度表是一张快照：它说的是'跑它的那天，这十一项有此效果'。它看不见的失败是第十二项——
有人给 plant 或 HAL 加了一个旋钮，表格照旧通过，而主张照旧被发表得好像新旋钮已被覆盖。README 的 L3 行靠这张
表支撑，所以'新旋钮必须入表'必须是一条门禁。
How it is checked (`gates.py budget`). Every `void set_<name>(` in `files` must appear either in
`covered` -- in which case the `StartupEffects` field it drives must appear in `covered_by`, so the
mapping cannot rot into a claim -- or in `not_an_error_source` with a written reason. A setter in
检查方式（`gates.py budget`）。`files` 里每一个 `void set_<name>(` 必须出现在 `covered` 中
（此时它驱动的 `StartupEffects` 字段必须出现在 `covered_by` 里，于是这层映射不会退化成一句声明），
或出现在带理由的 `not_an_error_source` 中。两者都不在 = 红。

A knob may be covered by a table other than `covered_by`: `covered` maps the setter to the field it drives, and `covered_in` overrides which file that field must appear in. Position quantisation is covered by the positioning budget table, not by the start-up sensitivity table, and both are tables under the same rule.

not_an_error_source.set_voltage_dq: the drive input, not an imperfection: it is what the controller commands.
not_an_error_source.set_voltage: the drive input of the phase-variable plant, same reason.
not_an_error_source.set_load_torque: an operating condition the claim is stated over, not a modelling error. The load-step series covers it as a sweep.
not_an_error_source.set_mechanical_speed: a test-double switch that freezes the mechanics (dyno mode), not a physical effect.
not_an_error_source.set_state: initial condition of the phase-variable plant, not an imperfection.
not_an_error_source.set_sensor_present: topology (sensored vs sensorless), not an error magnitude: it changes which claim applies rather than degrading a number.
not_an_error_source.set_offset_mech_rad: the alignment offset the library itself computes and hands over, not a plant imperfection.
not_an_error_source.set_index_position_mech_rad: presence and location of an index mark: topology, same reason as set_sensor_present.
not_an_error_source.set_voltage_v: the DC link setting, an operating condition.
not_an_error_source.set_deadtime_transition: shapes the same dead-time source rather than adding one: the table covers its magnitude with the ideal sign() model, which is the larger of the two because a smooth transition reduces the clamp.
not_an_error_source.set_inverter: attaches a different voltage path (switching model instead of mean value); the dead-time row covers that source, and two sources for one effect would make the number unreadable.
not_an_error_source.set_bus: attaches the bus meter: a *measurement port*, not an imperfection, and off by default. With no meter the DC-link voltage is the stiff constant it has always been, so no existing claim's sensitivity table can move.
not_an_error_source.set_meter: the same attachment, reached from the DC-link adapter instead of the plant HAL; it exists so that `voltage_v()` can read the node equation, and it is the same no-op-by-default as `set_bus`.
not_an_error_source.enable_mechanics: the rotor's inertia and damping are properties of the machine being modelled, not imperfections of the model, so the claim is stated over them rather than corrected for them. Swept where it matters: the 2J repeat in test_sil_motion_profile.cpp and the coast in test_sil_cogging.cpp.
not_an_error_source.set_thermal: the one-node winding model's Rt/Ct are machine parameters the caller supplies, not an imperfection the model pretends away -- and its effect is accounted for against closed forms rather than as a sensitivity dip: `test_sil_thermal.cpp` checks the settle, the time constant, the quadratic root of the Rs(T) feedback and the boundary past which no steady state exists, and the port adds exactly `0.0F` when off. No published claim rests on a temperature yet, because this port is the first thing in the repository that can produce one; if a derating claim ever does, it belongs in `covered` against that claim's table rather than here.
not_an_error_source.set_bus_current_a: A **measurement**, not an imperfection: the plant publishes the current the bus node carried over the period it just integrated, and the bench's link hands it to whoever asks. It injects nothing into the model -- the number is an output of the same `bus_current_a()` the meter books. What *would* be an error source is a shunt offset or a gain error, and neither exists here: the case that guards this is the energy identity in `test_sil_bus_current.cpp`, which fails if the published number is scaled, inverted or mis-averaged.
not_an_error_source.set_bus_current_unavailable: The absence of that measurement, which is the state a bench with no bus shunt is in -- it makes the link answer "not measured" rather than 0 A. Excluding it here is the same decision `temperature` and the optional contracts already have: an absent capability is a state to report, not an error to model.
not_an_error_source.set_velocity_supported: a contract case, not an imperfection: the HAL says a sensor may report an angle and no speed, and switching this off is how that case is reached. Nothing about the machine becomes wrong, so there is no sensitivity to measure -- what it changes is which of the two angle opinions exists, and `test_sil_angle_opinions.cpp` is where that is measured.
